Lessons.Title: Base-ten Diagrams to Represent Division
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will find the quotients of two-digit and three-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.
In grade 3, you used base-ten representations to help them reason about division of a two-digit number into equal-size groups. This lesson builds on that understanding and revisits it in the context of three-digit dividends. You recall that you can exchange or decompose one or more units of a higher place value for 10 units of the next lower place value in order to have enough units to put into equal groups.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Base-ten Diagrams (10 minutes); Activity 1: Divide with Diagrams or Blocks (15 minutes); Activity 2: Help Noah Get Unstuck (20 minutes); Cool-down: Find the Value of a Quotient (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens or 1 ten for 10 ones when base-ten diagrams need regrouping.

Edulytics authored model: Represent 235 as 2 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones. Regroup to 23 tens, share 20 tens among 5 groups (4 tens each). Regroup remaining 3 tens into 30 ones; 35 ones give 7 to each group. Answer 47.
First-party Cool-down: Represent 117 ÷ 3 with a base-ten diagram.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
